cards.explanation: The answer is a ringing gong or a clanging cymbal. Paul says, "If I speak in the tongues of men and of angels, but have not love, I am only a ringing gong or a clanging cymbal." Picture the loudest, most impressive speaker ever, and without love it's just NOISE. Even angel-language turns into a smoke alarm when love is missing.

The answer is nothing, and Paul doesn't soften it. Prophecy, all mysteries, all knowledge and faith to move mountains, and then he says, "…but have not love, I am nothing." Look at that list, friends. It's the whole trophy shelf, and love is the one thing that makes it count.

The answer is True, and it stings a little. Paul writes, "If I give all I possess to the poor and exult in the surrender of my body, but have not love, I gain nothing." Giving everything away is a big deal, and he's not saying it's small. He's saying love is what the giving has to carry.

The answer is that love does not envy. Paul says, "Love is patient, love is kind. It does not envy…" When somebody else gets the bigger blessing, love doesn't sit there counting. I'll be honest, I've seen a baker's cookie come out prettier than mine, and love says clap for them.

The answer is False. Paul writes that love "…is not rude, it is not self-seeking, it is not easily angered, it keeps no account of wrongs." Love isn't sitting there with its finger on the buzzer. Think of the calmest person you know in a traffic jam, and that's the direction Paul is pointing.

The answer is wrongs. Paul says love "…keeps no account of wrongs." Somebody does you dirty, and love doesn't file it away for later. I spent years in the back of a junk drawer, friends, and I can tell you, that's one pile of old receipts love never keeps.
The answer is the truth. Paul says love "…takes no pleasure in evil, but rejoices in the truth." Notice love has a happy side, too. It doesn't just turn away from evil, it celebrates what's true.

The answer is True. Paul says love "…bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things." Hopes ALL things, friends, not just the easy ones. That's four "all things" in a row, and he means every one.

The answer is that prophecies will cease. Paul says, "But where there are prophecies, they will cease; where there are tongues, they will be restrained; where there is knowledge, it will be dismissed." It's a long list, and love is the one on the other side of it. Right before, he says, "Love never fails."

The answer is perfect. Paul says, "…but when the perfect comes, the partial passes away." Just before, he said we know in part and we prophesy in part. So the partial is what gives way when the perfect arrives. Half a batch makes way for the whole thing.
The answer is False. Paul says, "When I became a man, I set aside childish ways." He talked, thought and reasoned like a child, and then he grew up. Something partial gave way to something fuller.

The answer is face to face. Paul says, "Now we see but a dim reflection as in a mirror; then we shall see face to face." Now it's a dim reflection, and then it's face to face. I think that's the part worth waiting for.

The answer is True. Paul says, "Now I know in part; then I shall know fully, even as I am fully known." Right now it's a piece. Then it's the whole picture, and he'll know fully, just as he is fully known.

The answer is love. Paul says, "And now these three remain: faith, hope, and love; but the greatest of these is love." Faith and hope stay too, friends, so it's a strong lineup. Still, he names love as the greatest.
